video_title: Steph Curry wants NO DRAMA amid Warriors contract extension talks | NBA Today

quotes.speaker: Shams Charania
quotes.summary_phrase: Stephen Curry's contract extension options with the Golden State Warriors
quotes.excerpt: The ball is totally in Stephen Curry's court.
quotes.quote: This is in a completely different place than the Carl Anthony Towns Knicks situation is at. The ball is totally in Stephen Curry's court. They have given him a slew of options to take. He has one-year deals, two-year deals, max deals, slightly under the max where he would be giving the team a discount, some more flexibility, and player option deals as well. So he has all the options, but another option that Stephen Curry has, not contractually right now, is potentially waiting into the season or waiting until next off-season when the Warriors, if Stephen Curry waits, would have about $100 million in cap space.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Brian Windhorst on Stephen Curry's contract extension strategy
quotes.excerpt: If Stephen Curry is willing to take less than the max contract, don't sign.

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: If Stephen Curry is willing to take less than the max contract, don't sign. If he wants the max, which he has absolutely earned 100 times over, sign. That's it. So if he doesn't sign, actions over words. He doesn't even have to say. We know that he might be open to taking less than the max. This just happened with Draymond Green. Draymond opted out of his contract, it was a little bit of a trial run for the Warriors. They were trying to sign LeBron James or other players, they weren't able to do that, and they gave Draymond the exact same money back. This is Steph potentially doing the same thing. If you don't sign, it opens up a world of possibilities.

text_blocks.speaker: Malika Andrews
text_blocks.text: But if he wants the money, no problem. Here you go, sign this afternoon. Very simple, no reason to compare it to the Carl Anthony Towns situation, no reason to make it more than a half-day story.

quotes.speaker: Anthony Slater
quotes.summary_phrase: Stephen Curry's commitment to the Golden State Warriors
quotes.excerpt: The reason that Steph did the interview with Slater is to reiterate his career-long commitment.
quotes.quote: The reason that Steph did the interview with Slater is to reiterate his career-long commitment to the Warriors. To nip in the bud any discussion that leaving is even a consideration for him. And so, no worry about that. Waiting is actually good news for Golden State because that shows a willingness to be flexible, to work with the front office to try to rebuild that thing into a contender, which I think there's a very narrow path for that to happen.

quotes.speaker: Richard Jefferson
quotes.summary_phrase: Richard Jefferson on Stephen Curry's winning mentality
quotes.excerpt: I expect Steph to do this. He's a winner.
quotes.quote: I expect Steph to do this. He's a winner. We saw and complimented Jaylen Brunson for doing this. All the guys that do stuff like this take a little bit of a cut and make sure that they go out there and win. Always loved them. Steph, we've had our battles, but go get your money if you're going to get it. If not, I hope you go out winning and doing your thing in the playoffs and not having to be on a team that's just not competitive.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Brian Windhorst on Stephen Curry's desire for team efficiency
quotes.excerpt: The Warriors aren't good enough to let Steph turn the ball over like crazy.
quotes.quote: Steve recently talked with Stephen Curry and he said, 'Hey, for years, decades, I've been not getting on Draymond, you Draymond and Steph about turnovers. That's over.' It's frankly the Warriors aren't good enough to let Steph turn the ball over like crazy. And he also said he wanted Draymond to shoot a bunch of threes, which Draymond said no one's ever told him before. So it looks like the Warriors are trying to figure out the, forget about the contract stuff. On the court, they're trying to figure out a pathway, how can we get ourselves to the play-in.

quotes.speaker: Richard Jefferson
quotes.summary_phrase: Richard Jefferson on the impact of Stephen Curry and Draymond Green
quotes.excerpt: Part of playing against Steph and Draymond, you know that they're going to have three turnovers.
quotes.quote: Part of playing against Steph and Draymond, you know that they're going to have three turnovers, but it has no weight. They're going to have four turnovers, but it has no weight. If I come in a game, or one of the other guys on our team at the time would have came in and they have three turnovers, it's different because we don't play like that. They played like that their whole careers. They play free flow, so it made them dangerous. To hear about an efficient Stephen Curry, an efficient Draymond Green, I don't even know what that looks like, but I know it takes the danger down and it lets me know that they're getting up there in age.
